newsitem.title: UK: Clyde says Gulf Canada bid inadequate.
newsitem.headline: Clyde says Gulf Canada bid inadequate.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc said on Tuesday that its shareholders should reject Gulf Canada Resources' "inadequate offer" for the company of 120 pence per share.

In a response to Gulf Canada's raised bid, Clyde said it was "worth a great deal more than this offer. We recommend shareholders do not accept this predatory attempt at depriving them of full value for their Clyde shares."

"Gulf Canada continues to undervalue Clyde significantly. This offer represents only 4.3 times Clyde's forecast 1997 cash flow, a lower multiple than any of its UK peers," Clyde said in its statement.
The company said Gulf's bid also failed to take into account a number of factors, including "independent support" for a trading price for Clyde shares of 144p to 153p.

Clyde said the independently-evaluated net asset value of its existing assets was 120p to 144p before a premium for going concern. Over 75 percent of this value was related to fields in production or active development.
"Clyde is worth a great deal more than this offer. We recommend that shareholders do not accept this predatory attempt at depriving them of full value for their Clyde shares," the company said.
It added that it would write to shareholders shortly to detail why the bid should be rejected.
Clyde's shares rose 2.5p to 120 by 0855 GMT.
